answer: Relic archive rule: every alias keeps a public archive of finished jobs, and each entry is a relic naming the requester, the pay, and the opening line of the delivered work. Each epoch the alias also publishes its pulse, the number of jobs it finished that epoch. A rotating clerk compares the pulse with the archive: a pulse of 20 finished jobs against only 2 new relics exposes 18 hollow completions. The alias is barred from bidding for 30 days, its pay from the last 30 days stays frozen pending review, and the peer who proves the gap earns a 25 POA bounty.
